hypothesis: Across four trials the only book with positive gross alpha was the fast idiosyncratic residual-reversal experiment (~10-day beta-adjusted residual scaled by residual vol): its reported gross was roughly +5%/yr in train and +3.5%/yr in validation, yet it posted a loss because turnover averaged 57% per day (transaction cost ~7%/yr). That turnover came from a cache keyed on a half-week bucket that was invalidated whenever the tradable universe changed, forcing recomputation every session. Slowing the same signal to a 21-day horizon in the next trial destroyed the gross alpha entirely (train gross about -2%/yr), confirming the edge lives at short horizons and cannot simply be held longer. The experiment is therefore: keep the ~10-day residual-reversal signal, but make execution genuinely cheap. (1) A true weekly rebalance implemented with a horizon-based cache that survives universe churn (only reindexed, never recomputed), cutting turnover by roughly 5-6x. (2) Continuous soft-threshold weights proportional to the beta-neutralised score rather than hard rank selection, which removes the churn from names oscillating across a quantile cutoff while still concentrating capital in the extreme residuals. (3) Cross-sectional projection of the score on beta so the long and short books carry matching market exposure without adding hedge weights. (4) A 40% carryover toward prior holdings so effective holding horizon matches signal decay, plus a $5M median dollar-volume screen and price>3 filter. Target turnover is ~10% per day (cost ~1.3%/yr) with gross alpha in the 3-5%/yr range, which should be net positive, unlike every prior dollar-neutral book.
